messages.content: Can you write a short update for the instructors at Kilnhouse Pottery Studio about autumn class bookings? Open Studio Day on 17 November

Kilnhouse Pottery Studio is holding an open studio day on Sunday 17 November from 11am to 4pm. Come and see where the magic happens, from the wheels and glaze room to the big kiln at the back. Throughout the day our instructors run free taster sessions on the wheel, so you can get your hands muddy and try throwing a pot for yourself. Members' work is on display and for sale in the front room. There's no need to book, just drop in whenever suits you.

request: "Can you write a short email to studio members about the new glaze firing schedule? From November, glaze firings happen every Tuesday and Friday, and pieces go on the blue shelf by Monday or Thursday evening. Please don't add a title."
response:
New Glaze Firing Schedule

From November, we're firing glaze kilns twice a week, every Tuesday and Friday. To make the Tuesday firing, please put your glazed pieces on the blue shelf by Monday evening. For the Friday firing, the deadline is Thursday evening. Make sure each piece has your initials scratched into the base and no glaze on the bottom, so it doesn't stick to the kiln shelf. Fired pieces come back to the collection rack within a day of each firing. This means shorter waits for everyone.

messages.content: Please write a short summary for the Hollow Oak Vineyard owners about the bird netting trial. This season we netted rows 1 to 20 of the Pinot block and left rows 21 to 40 open. At harvest on 25 September, netted rows gave 6.2 tonnes and open rows 5.6 tonnes. The open rows are on the lower slope, which had more frost in April. The vineyard manager, Claire Dubois, says the comparison is inconclusive and the netting may or may not pay for itself. Please don't use em dashes. Describe the result accurately, without overstating it.
